source_text: Στίχ. α΄, β΄, ι΄, ιε΄. Λοιδορήσασα Μαριὰμ τὸν Μωσέα, ἐλεπρώθη, ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς γενομένη ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας καθίσασα. Τοῦτο δὲ γέγονε πρὸς φόβον τοῦ λαοῦ. Εἰ γὰρ τῆς ἀδελφῆς οὐκ ἐφείσατο, οὐδὲ ἑτέρου.
thought_title: Miriam's leprosy as a warning to the people
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 12, where Miriam spoke against Moses and was struck with leprosy.
pass_a_gloss: Verses 1, 2, 10, 15. Miriam, having reviled Moses, was struck with leprosy, having been outside the camp for seven days, having sat. But this happened for the fear of the people. For if he did not spare his sister, neither will he spare another.

choices.why: Captures the active verbal abuse against Moses, stronger than merely speaking against.
Matches the glossary rendering and preserves the passive force of the punishment.
Keeps the participle construction and the glossary term 'camp'.

choices.english: for the fear of the people
choices.why: Preserves the purpose nuance of πρός with accusative.
rejected: as a warning to the people

choices.why: Keeps the elliptical future sense implied by the conditional, matching the force of the Greek.

bible_refs.note: ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς γενομένη ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας

pass_b_english: When Miriam reviled Moses, she was struck with leprosy and sat outside the camp for seven days (Numbers 12:15). This happened for the fear of the people. For if he did not spare his sister, neither will he spare another.

last_rejected.source_quote: Λοιδορήσασα Μαριὰμ τὸν Μωσέα, ἐλεπρώθη, ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς γενομένη ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας καθίσασα.
last_rejected.why: The passage describes Miriam’s leprosy and seven‑day isolation, which is in Numbers 12:10‑11, not 12:15.
last_rejected.fix: Replace the citation with “(Numbers 12:10‑11)” and note the Septuagint numbering if needed.
last_rejected.ruling: Source cites Στίχ. ιε΄ (v.15); Numbers 12:15 records Miriam's seven-day isolation outside camp, matching the text.
